Few careers make their purpose as visible as civil engineering. Bridges, roads, and public spaces caught my attention early because of the way they shape everyday life, and that fascination has grown into a clear commitment to designing infrastructure that is resilient and genuinely useful to the communities it serves. Originally from Sri Lanka, I have pursued that commitment through advanced study and practice, completing a Master’s degree at a university ranked in the global top 500. Through my studies and project work, I have developed my understanding of how technical decisions affect safety, cost, and long-term performance, and I have completed 4 projects with tangible outcomes. In particular, civil engineering appeals to me because it brings together problem-solving, creativity, and public impact in a form people use every day.

Through my studies and professional experience, I have become especially interested in turning complex technical requirements into practical, buildable solutions that can be carried forward clearly across contractors, planners, and clients. One area that reflects this was learning a new digital design and analysis tool: rather than mastering it quickly, I built confidence with it over more than a year of regular use, revisiting drawings, checking outputs, and gradually using it more independently on live work. In another instance, I noticed that repeated delays were coming from the way design queries were being logged and passed between teams, so I introduced a simpler tracking sheet and response sequence that reduced back-and-forth and saved time for the wider team. Beyond my immediate remit, colleagues across the organisation, including senior staff, have regularly asked for my input on difficult technical questions when they wanted an additional view before decisions were made. During one extended project phase, I stayed with a demanding package of work through several setbacks, including revisions and deadline pressure, and added extra hours when needed to keep deliverables moving.

One moment that brought the profession into personal focus came on a family road trip when we crossed a bridge I had helped deliver. My relatives insisted on stopping for a photo, joking that it was the only holiday landmark where I could explain the drainage system in detail; for me, it captured exactly why this work matters. Overall, I am ready to bring my background, judgement, and commitment to practical infrastructure into my next Civil Engineer role.

Numbers rarely speak for themselves; what draws me to data analysis is the process of uncovering the story inside them and turning that story into decisions that are both smarter and more human-centred. This has shaped my career direction and confirmed my desire to work as a Data Analyst, combining analytical thinking with practical business impact. I am originally from France, and I hold a Doctorate from a university ranked in the global top 100. Through that academic training, and through completing 6 projects with tangible outcomes, I developed a strong interest in translating complex datasets into clear, actionable narratives so that both technical and non-technical stakeholders can see what matters and decide what to do next. Even in everyday life, this instinct appears naturally: during a family dinner, I once settled a playful debate about who was always late by building a quick chart from old message timestamps, and my family still jokes that no conversation is safe from becoming a dashboard.

My professional experience has shown me what this looks like in practice. When my team adopted an unfamiliar method, I learned it within a few weeks and soon found myself walking colleagues through how to use it in their own work. On another project, I faced a problem my group had treated as unsolvable; after testing a different approach, I developed a new method that solved it, and other teams later began using the same approach. I am also regularly asked by colleagues across the organisation, including senior staff, to weigh in on difficult questions outside my immediate remit, particularly when they need a clear interpretation of complex information. In a separate long-running assignment, I stayed with the work through repeated obstacles and changing demands, putting in additional time where needed until it was completed.

These experiences have given me a grounded understanding of how careful analysis can support better decisions, stronger communication, and meaningful results. I am excited to bring that approach to a Data Analyst role and continue growing through work that turns raw data into insight, direction, and impact.
